note: The LEGO grid. A module is the stud pitch; Technic holes sit on the same pitch. LDraw coordinates (LDU) are exact multiples of these, so every position in ldraw-geometry.json converts to modules by dividing by 20.

ldu_mm.note: The LDraw specification's real-world approximation; taken because every LDraw file is drawn on it.

alt.note: Measured on real bricks (±0.0001 mm). 0.2 % smaller: 0.2 mm over a 15-module beam.

ldraw_axes.value: right-handed, -Y is up; X to the right and Z towards the viewer in LDraw's front view; each part has its own origin

module_mm.note: 20 LDU x 0.4 mm: the stud pitch and the Technic hole pitch.

brick_and_two_plates_mm.note: 24 + 8 + 8 LDU = 40 LDU = 2 modules: a brick and two plates stacked put Technic holes on the same 8 mm pitch vertically as horizontally.

pin_hole_diameter_mm.note: The hole cylinder has radius 6 LDU.

pin_hole_pitch_mm.note: Beam 7: holes every 20 LDU along its length.

axle_cross_mm.note: Across the cross of a Technic axle (LDraw bounding box 12 LDU).

axle_length_mm.note: An axle n long is 20 n - 1 LDU (axle 4: 79 LDU = 31.6 mm).

beam_thick_mm.note: A thick (studless) beam is 1 module along its holes' axis and 7.2 mm (0.9 module) across; n holes long it measures 8 n - 0.8 mm.

beam_thin_mm.note: A thin beam is half a module thick.

half_module_offsets.value: Thin beams (0.5 module thick), the 0.5-module bush 32123b, the pin 3/4, and the axle 5.5 with stop sit on half-module positions; EV3 parts put their holes on whole modules except where ldraw-geometry.json lists a hole centre at an odd multiple of 10 LDU.
